content: Coconut oil, also referred to as coconut butter, is a tropical oil with a wide range of uses. It is derived from copra, which is dried coconut meat. The term copra originates from the Malayalam word kopra, meaning dried coconut. The Philippines, the largest global exporter of coconut oil, generates 7% of its total export income from this product. Coconut oil was first developed as a commercial product in the 1860s by merchants in the South Seas and South Asia. Physical Properties Coconut oil is composed of approximately 90% saturated fat. It predominantly contains medium-chain triglycerides (MCTs), with about 92% saturated fatty acids, 6% monounsaturated fatty acids, and 2% polyunsaturated fatty acids. Among its saturated fatty acids, it includes 2% palmitic acid and 8% caprylic acid, along with five other saturated fatty acids. Its only monounsaturated fatty acid is oleic acid, and its only polyunsaturated fatty acid is linoleic acid. Unrefined coconut oil melts at 24–25°C (76°F) and has a smoke point of 170°C (350°F), while refined coconut oil has a higher smoke point of 232°C (450°F). Due to its high saturated fat content, coconut oil is highly stable, resists oxidation, and can last up to two years without becoming rancid. Health Effects Heart Disease Medical research has established that consuming saturated fats can increase the risk of cardiovascular disease. Since coconut oil is rich in saturated fats, regular consumption may elevate this risk. However, a 2004 study published in Clinical Biochemistry found that virgin coconut oil reduced LDL cholesterol (associated with cardiovascular disease) while increasing beneficial HDL cholesterol levels. An epidemiological study in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition examined two indigenous populations whose diets derived 63% and 34% of their energy from coconuts, respectively, and found no increased risk of cardiovascular disease. Another 2004 article in the same journal suggested that the presumed causal link between saturated fats and heart disease might be a statistical error. Other studies have indicated that coconut oil may aid in weight loss and recovery from poisoning. Antimicrobial Effects A study conducted at University College Hospital in Ibadan, Nigeria, and published in the Journal of Medicinal Food demonstrated that coconut oil effectively killed certain strains of Candida, the fungus responsible for candidiasis in humans. The researchers recommended coconut oil as a treatment for fungal infections. Types of Coconut Oil Virgin Coconut Oil Virgin coconut oil is extracted from fresh coconuts rather than dried copra. It is typically produced using one of three methods: 1. Quick drying: Fresh coconut meat is quickly dried and then pressed to extract the oil. 2. Wet-milling: Oil is extracted from fresh coconut meat without prior drying. Coconut milk is first expressed by pressing, and the oil is then separated from the water using methods such as boiling, fermentation, refrigeration, enzymes, or mechanical centrifuge. 3. Direct micro expelling: Oil is extracted from fresh coconut meat after adjusting the water content, followed by pressing the coconut flesh to directly obtain free-flowing oil. Unlike olive oil, there is no global standard or governing body that defines or regulates the classification of coconut oil as virgin. However, the Philippines has established a governmental standard through its Department of Science and Technology (DOST). Refined Coconut Oil Refined coconut oil, known in the industry as RBD (refined, bleached, and deodorized) coconut oil, is made from copra, the dried coconut meat. Copra can be dried using smoke, sunlight, or kilns. The unrefined oil extracted from copra, called crude coconut oil, is not suitable for consumption and must be refined. Hydrogenated Coconut Oil Coconut oil is often partially or fully hydrogenated to increase its melting point in warmer climates. This process increases the saturated fat content and may produce trans fats. Fractionated Coconut Oil Fractionated coconut oil is a processed form in which most long-chain triglycerides are removed, leaving only saturated fats. It is also referred to as caprylic/capric triglyceride or medium-chain triglyceride (MCT) oil, as it primarily contains caprylic and capric acids. Being fully saturated, fractionated oil is more heat-stable than other forms of coconut oil and has an almost indefinite shelf life. Applications Cooking Coconut oil is widely used in cooking, particularly for frying. In regions where coconut oil is a staple, refined oil is the most commonly used type. It is also frequently used to flavor South Asian curries. Manufacturing Coconut oil is used in large quantities for producing margarine, soap, and cosmetics. Hydrogenated or partially hydrogenated coconut oil is often found in non-dairy creamers and snack foods. Fractionated coconut oil is used in the production of essences, massage oils, and cosmetics. Additionally, coconut oil is a key component in industrial lubricants, such as those used in the cold rolling of steel strips. Cosmetics and Skin Treatments Coconut oil is an excellent skin moisturizer and softener. Studies have shown that extra virgin coconut oil is as effective and safe as mineral oil when used as a moisturizer, with no adverse reactions reported. While unsuitable for use with condoms, coconut oil is an inexpensive and effective lubricant for sexual intercourse, though it may cause allergic reactions in some individuals. In India and Sri Lanka, coconut oil is commonly used for hair styling and to cool or soothe the scalp. In Tamil Nadu and other coastal regions like Kerala, Karnataka, Maharashtra, and Goa, people often apply coconut oil to their entire body before bathing in warm water to maintain healthy skin, hair, and overall body health. As a Fuel Traditional Use Coconut oil has been traditionally used in oil lamps. Diesel Engines Coconut oil has been tested as a feedstock for biodiesel to power diesel engines, including generators and transport vehicles. It can be blended to create biodiesel or used directly without blending. However, B100 biodiesel blends (100% biodiesel) are only feasible in temperate climates due to the oil's gel point of approximately 10°C (50°F). Raw coconut oil must meet the Weihenstephan standard for pure vegetable oil used as fuel; otherwise, unmodified engines may suffer from coking and clogging. Stationary engines with continuous loads exceeding 70% may be used without modifications, though opinions on this vary. The physical constraints of using raw coconut oil in diesel engines include its higher viscosity (up to 10 times that of diesel), which alters fuel spray patterns and stresses the injection pump, and the need for a minimum combustion chamber temperature of 500°C to prevent fuel polymerization, which can clog injectors and damage engine components. Additionally, its solidification point of 22–25°C necessitates a fuel tank heater in temperate climates. Remote communities with abundant coconut supplies and milling capacity can use raw coconut oil to generate electricity, provided diesel engines are adapted. Coconut oil is currently used as a transport fuel in the Philippines, and research into its potential as an electricity source is ongoing in Pacific islands. During the Bougainville conflict in the 1990s, islanders used coconut oil to fuel vehicles when cut off from supplies due to a blockade. Aircraft Fuel In February 2008, a mixture of coconut oil and babassu oil was used to partially power one engine of a Boeing 747 during a biofuel trial sponsored by Virgin Atlantic. Philippine Innovations On January 16, 2008, a company in the Philippines converted coconut oil into engine oil using Korean biotechnology. Rey Mangio, managing director of Chun Hae Food Processor in Davao City, unveiled the S-9 lubricating motor oil for gasoline and diesel engines. Since 2005, over 400 vehicles have tested the product at a 20% blend rate of crankcase capacity. Chemical analyses revealed that the product reduces fuel consumption by up to 45%, decreases smoke emissions by up to 95%, increases engine power, and lowers operating temperatures. The company produces 5,000 liters of motor oil per month.
